page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The processor is supported by 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps. No local storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core and multi-core Geekbench metrics, software compilation with Clang, and text processing. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top tier. Multi-threaded decompression, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, and Redis SET operations show strong results. Memory performance is highly polarized: cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong, whereas uncached large-block read and write operations fall into the average category. Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput are exceptionally high, while LLM inference speeds for small and medium models remain average.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated compute resources, the c9g.8xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that benefit from high core density without requiring massive memory-to-CPU ratios. The 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, but the high-speed Neoverse-V3 cores offset this for processing-heavy tasks. This server is highly suited for software compilation, static web serving, database operations, text processing, and multi-threaded decompression workloads.
